purpose: Reviewed allowlist of every line by which the composed production Firestore Rules differ from what production main deploys. 2.5.1 (main 23bdd439) deploys the R93-07 LOCK MY SIGNINGS Rules; the hunks below are R93-08 (Rules budget sweep: same-check slims of JOIN, Transfer War START and the season commit). Regenerate only with node tests/support/composed-production-rules.cjs --print-main-delta origin/main, then review every hunk.

hunks.why: START slim: the role-list helper is no longer needed once START tests each role list as exactly [] (the only value START allows).

added: // R93-08 (Rules budget sweep): JOIN (the redeem) is the costliest write of the game (~991 of the 1,000 expressions on
// the rivalry document). Each branch now tests the joined slot first, so the branch for the other slot stops after one
// comparison. The stored open slot is compared with the one map validOpenSlot accepts (all seven keys must be there,
// since validOpenSlot reads every one of them, and each has exactly one allowed value), which is the same check for
// far fewer expressions. Every other check is unchanged, so the same JOINs pass and fail.
hunks.why: JOIN slim comment: why the open slot is compared with one map literal and the joined slot is tested first.

added: // R93-08 (Rules budget sweep): JOIN (the redeem) spent ~991 of the 1,000 expressions on this document, most of it on

// stored connectionState that validRivalryRedeem requires anyway, so every other update skips it after one test. The
// three branches are the same; only their order and that first test changed, so the same updates pass and fail.
hunks.why: JOIN reorder comment: why the redeem branch now comes before the Terminal Close branch.
JOIN reorder: the same three update branches; redeem now before Terminal Close and starting with the stored 'pending-pair' it requires anyway.
